best_architecture: Use a polyglot-persistence 'right store for the right access pattern' architecture with three specialized backends behind a single async orchestration layer, exactly matching Local-Claw's Mongo+Chroma+Redis design. (1) MongoDB as the source-of-truth document store for sessions, messages, and tool calls. Model a session as a parent document with an embedded array of messages ONLY if the conversation is bounded; for long-running agent sessions prefer a referenced model with a separate `messages` collection keyed by `session_id` to avoid the 16MB BSON document cap and unbounded-array anti-pattern. Recommended collections: `sessions` (metadata, status, model, token budget, created/updated), `messages` (session_id, role, content, parent_msg_id, timestamps, indexed on {session_id:1, seq:1}), `tool_calls` (session_id, message_id, tool_name, args, result, status, latency_ms, error). Index on the fields you filter/sort by; use a partial index for any outbox/pending flags. Apply TTL indexes or a scheduled archival job for stale sessions. (2) Chroma (or Qdrant — see SOTA) as the long-term semantic/episodic memory store. Chroma is the correct default for a single-node RunPod A6000 deployment: it is lightweight, Python-first, embeds cleanly in the asyncio orchestrator via AsyncHttpClient (client-server mode, not in-process, so the embedding store survives orchestrator restarts), and is sufficient for tens-to-hundreds of thousands of vectors. Store the canonical record in Mongo and store ONLY the vector + a minimal metadata payload + the Mongo `_id` in Chroma, so Chroma is a rebuildable index, never a source of truth. (3) Redis (redis.asyncio) for task queues, caching, and ephemeral working memory. For skill task dispatch use Redis Streams with consumer groups (XADD/XREADGROUP/XACK) rather than LIST LPUSH/BRPOP: Streams give at-least-once delivery, explicit ACK, automatic retry of un-ACKed messages via the pending-entries-list, a dead-letter path, and multi-consumer fan-out — all of which a bare BRPOP list lacks (a worker crash after BRPOP silently loses the task). Keep a LIST only if you need a trivial single-consumer hot path. Use Redis also for the response/result cache and short-lived working-memory keys with TTLs. CONNECTION POOLING: instantiate exactly ONE shared AsyncIOMotorClient, ONE Chroma AsyncHttpClient, and ONE redis.asyncio client (or one ConnectionPool) at orchestrator startup and reuse them for the process lifetime — never create clients per request/per task. Each client owns its own pool (Motor default maxPoolSize=100; tune minPoolSize>0 to pre-warm, set maxIdleTimeMS and waitQueueTimeoutMS to bound blocking). Close all three on graceful shutdown. CROSS-STORE ATOMICITY: the Mongo+Chroma+Redis writes are NOT a distributed transaction — accept eventual consistency and make Mongo the single source of truth. Use the transactional-outbox pattern: write the business record and an embedded/colocated outbox marker in one atomic single-document Mongo write, then have a background worker (driven by a Mongo Change Stream or polling a partial index of pending markers) project that record into Chroma and enqueue Redis tasks. Make all downstream Chroma upserts and Redis consumers idempotent (use the Mongo `_id` as the Chroma id and as a dedup/idempotency key) so at-least-once delivery and retries never corrupt state. This gives crash-safe, rebuildable indices without 2PC.
reference_papers: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems (Packer et al. 2023) - arxiv:2310.08560 - OS-inspired hierarchical/virtual-memory paging between in-context and external storage; the canonical model for tiering working memory vs. persisted long-term memory across stores

Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior (Park et al. 2023) - arxiv:2304.03442 - memory-stream architecture with retrieval (recency+importance+relevance), reflection, and planning; foundational for vector-backed episodic memory layout

Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory (Chhikara, Khant et al. 2025) - arxiv:2504.19413 - production memory layer combining a structured store with a vector index; directly relevant to Mongo-as-record + Chroma-as-index split

Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory (Rasmussen et al. 2025) - arxiv:2501.13956 - temporal knowledge-graph backend for agent memory; relevant for schema/temporal modeling of sessions and facts
A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents (Xu et al. 2025) - arxiv:2502.12110 - dynamic, self-organizing agentic memory store design
HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for LLMs (Gutierrez et al. 2024) - NeurIPS 2024 - retrieval/indexing design for long-term memory over a vector + graph store
Memory in the Age of AI Agents: A Survey (Hu, Liu, Yue et al. 2025) - arxiv:2512.13564 - broad survey of storage backends and short-/long-term memory separation across agent systems [uncertain]
From Human Memory to AI Memory: A Survey on Memory Mechanisms in the Era of LLMs (Wu et al. 2025) - arxiv:2504.15965 - taxonomy of memory mechanisms and storage strategies

Long-MemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory (Wu, Wang et al. 2024, ICLR 2025) - arxiv:2410.10813 - benchmark to validate that a Mongo+Chroma session-memory design actually recalls across sessions
reference_repos: redis/agent-memory-server - production-grade memory server for agents/AI apps built on Redis providing persistent storage, vector search, working/long-term memory split, ACK-based task semantics, plus LangChain/LangGraph-compatible tools; closest reference for the Redis layer of a hybrid store - https://github.com/redis/agent-memory-server

rohitg00/agentmemory - persistent memory for coding agents: SHA-256 dedup, privacy/secret stripping, LLM compression to structured facts, hybrid BM25 + vector index, Ebbinghaus-style decay/auto-eviction; good reference for the ingest pipeline and dedup/idempotency keys - https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory

mem0ai/mem0 - widely used scalable long-term memory layer for agents; pluggable vector stores (Chroma/Qdrant/pgvector) + structured metadata store, reference for the record-vs-index separation - https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0
getzep/zep - temporal knowledge-graph memory server for agents; reference for temporal session/fact schema and a service-based memory backend - https://github.com/getzep/zep
chroma-core/chroma - the Chroma vector DB itself; client-server mode + AsyncHttpClient is the embeddable local vector store for Local-Claw - https://github.com/chroma-core/chroma
mongodb/motor - official async (asyncio) MongoDB driver; the connection-pooling reference for the document layer - https://github.com/mongodb/motor
qdrant/qdrant - Rust vector DB; reference/alternative if Chroma's filtering or scale becomes limiting (see SOTA) - https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant
key_libraries: motor - Python (async) - >=3.6 (3.7.x current) - official asyncio MongoDB driver (AsyncIOMotorClient); single shared client, built-in PyMongo connection pool; note: newer PyMongo offers a native async API that may eventually supersede Motor [uncertain]
pymongo - Python - >=4.9 - underlying driver/BSON + pool implementation Motor builds on; pin alongside motor

chromadb - Python - >=0.5 / 1.x - vector store with chromadb.AsyncHttpClient for async client-server access; pin >=1.0.x carefully due to a reported AsyncHttpClient 422/get_or_create regression in early 1.0.0 [uncertain]

redis - Python (async) - >=5.0 (redis-py, includes redis.asyncio) - async Redis client with built-in async ConnectionPool; use redis.asyncio.Redis / from_url, requires explicit aclose() on shutdown (no async GC); supersedes the deprecated aioredis
qdrant-client - Python - latest - async-capable client if migrating/augmenting Chroma with Qdrant for advanced metadata filtering and scale (optional alternative)

sentence-transformers - Python - latest - generate embeddings locally on the A6000 to feed Chroma/Qdrant without an external embedding API (optional but recommended for a local-only stack) [uncertain]

celery or rq - Python - latest - higher-level Redis-backed task-queue frameworks if you prefer not to hand-roll Redis Streams consumer groups for skill dispatch (optional alternative to raw XADD/XREADGROUP)
